Owe Jacksonville Property Tax? Get a Cash Offer

We buy Jacksonville houses as-is. The title company pays unpaid tax from the proceeds.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026. Citations come from the Florida statutes and the official county and city pages linked in Sources. Where we could not confirm something on an official page, we say so.

Jacksonville property tax is billed by the Duval County tax collector, and Florida bills are due November 1 and delinquent April 1. This guide points you to the official Duval County offices and explains what happens to the tax when you sell.

Who bills what in Jacksonville

Jacksonville is in Duval County.

  • Duval County Property Appraiser (Jacksonville.gov) sets the assessed value and handles exemptions such as homestead.
  • Duval County Tax Collector (Jim Overton) sends the bill and collects the tax.
  • The clerk's Official Records search shows recorded deeds, liens and mortgages.

Due dates and discounts

Florida taxes are due November 1, or when the certified roll reaches the tax collector, and become delinquent April 1. Early payment discounts run 4 percent in November, 3 percent in December, 2 percent in January and 1 percent in February (Fla. Stat. 197.162 and 197.333). Real property is assessed as of January 1. Local notes from the county offices:

  • Important Dates page states: property taxes due with 4% discount on November 30, 2026 (4% discount for current real estate and tangible personal property paid by the last day of November).
  • Duval Property Appraiser page says 2025 tax bills were mailed on or about November 1, 2025 and that VAB petitioners must pay before the delinquency date (usually April 1).

Homestead and local notes

  • Homestead: deadline to file timely for the 2027 tax roll is March 1, 2027; late filing permitted through early September (25th day after TRIM notices are mailed in mid-August).

The city millage rate

We could not confirm the current Jacksonville millage rate on an opened official page, so we do not state one. Use the property appraiser's millage chart and the tax collector's parcel lookup for your bill.

Behind on Jacksonville property tax?
We buy Jacksonville houses as-is, and the title company pays unpaid tax from the proceeds.
Get My Cash Offer →

What we could not confirm

  • Full discount schedule below 4% (3%, 2%, 1% months) not stated on any Duval page opened.
  • Delinquency date and installment plan not confirmed on the opened Duval Tax Collector pages (the property-taxes page returned no extractable content).
  • Current tax certificate sale date not confirmed on a current Tax Collector page.

How to sell a house in Jacksonville when you owe property tax

  1. Find out what the title company needs. For an inherited or transferred house, that usually means the recorded document that shows who owns it today.
  2. Ask the tax collector for the amount due in the month you expect to close. Unpaid tax is paid from the sale proceeds at closing.
  3. Compare offers on what you net after repairs, commissions and closing costs, not on the headline price.
  4. If you want a fast, simple closing, ask for a written cash offer. We buy houses as-is. See selling a house in Jacksonville and we buy houses in Florida.

What a cash sale of a Jacksonville house looks like, step by step

People often ask what actually happens after they contact a cash buyer. Here is the usual order of events for a house in Jacksonville.

  1. Tell us about the property. Use the form on this page or call or text (424) 435-2326. We ask about the address, the condition and what is going on, such as a mortgage, back taxes, tenants or an estate.
  2. Get a written cash offer. We review the details and send a written offer. There is no obligation, and you can turn it down and owe us nothing.
  3. Pick your closing date. You choose the timeline. Some owners need weeks to move out, and others want to close quickly.
  4. The title company handles the paperwork. It checks ownership, pays off any mortgage and any unpaid property tax from the proceeds, and records the deed.
  5. You receive the proceeds. Our offers carry no agent commission, no fees and no closing costs to you.

Documents and information to have ready

You do not need everything below to get an offer, but each item makes the sale smoother and helps the title company work faster.

  • The deed or other proof of who owns the property today.
  • A recent mortgage statement or a payoff figure from the lender.
  • The latest property tax bill, plus any notice of unpaid or delinquent tax.
  • Homeowners association details, including dues and any unpaid assessments, if there is an association.
  • Current leases and the tenants' contact information, if the house is rented.
  • Estate paperwork, such as letters from the court, if you inherited the house.
  • A short list of known repairs. We buy as-is, but honest information avoids surprises.

Listing, selling it yourself or a cash offer: how they compare

Listing with an agent can bring a higher headline price when a house is in good shape and you have time. You pay the commission agreed in your listing contract, and you usually handle repairs, showings and the buyer's inspection requests. Closing depends on the buyer's financing.

Selling it yourself saves the listing commission but puts the marketing, the paperwork and the required Florida disclosures on you. You still need a title company or attorney to close.

Taking a cash offer trades some of the headline price for speed and certainty. We buy as-is, so there are no repairs, no showings and no financing contingency. It tends to fit owners dealing with foreclosure pressure, an inherited house, back taxes, tenants or a move on a deadline. Compare every option on what you net after repairs, fees and carrying costs, not on the headline price.

Questions to ask before you sell in Jacksonville

  • Ask the tax collector what is owed and what the title company will need at closing.
  • Ask your lender for a written payoff figure good through your expected closing date, and ask whether there is a prepayment penalty.
  • Ask the county assessor whether a pending appeal or exemption affects the bill, and whether any exemption you receive ends when you sell.
  • If the house was inherited, ask the title company which court documents it needs before it will insure the sale.
  • If tenants live in the house, check the lease for its end date and any notice you must give.

These are general questions to start a conversation, not legal advice. Rules in Florida change, so confirm details with the official office or a Florida attorney or tax professional.

How fast can I close on a cash sale?

You choose the closing date within what the title company needs to clear ownership and payoffs.

Do I have to clean out or repair the house?

No. We buy houses as-is, so you do not need to make repairs before selling.

Will you buy a house that has tenants in it?

Yes. We buy rentals as-is, occupied or vacant. Tell us about the lease when you request an offer.

What if I owe more on the mortgage than the house is worth?

Tell us the payoff figure. A sale that does not cover the loan may need lender approval, so ask your lender about a short sale before you sign anything.

Can I sell an inherited house before probate is finished?

It depends on who has legal authority to sign. The title company can tell you what court paperwork it needs.

Is there any cost to request an offer?

No. Requesting an offer is free and carries no obligation.

March 1 each year with the county property appraiser (Fla. Stat. 196.011).
